adversarialFinding.finding: The branch hostile tests and prior receipt claimed hardened Postal semantics, but the actual postal-effect-adapter.mjs on the branch still contained the old implementation: HTTP 409 in definite rejection, no bounded dispatch timeout, no one-click unsubscribe support, executionId required for reconciliation, and bounce mapped to reconciled rejection.
adversarialFinding.resolution: Replaced the stale adapter implementation with the already-reviewed hardened 1.1.0 donor semantics while preserving current-main authority boundaries. Existing source mutation guards now bind directly to the corrected implementation.

implemented: HTTP 409 removed from definite rejection statuses and therefore remains UNCERTAIN.
Bounded AbortController timeout added with one provider-call site and no hidden retry.
HTTPS one-click List-Unsubscribe support added with header injection protection.
Reconciliation can recover deterministic tag/message identity from providerEffectIdentity without requiring executionId, while contradictory supplied executionId remains ambiguous.
Authenticated Postal webhook provenance is required before reconciliation can settle an uncertain effect.
Webhook Message-ID mismatch is ambiguous rather than accepted.
Bounce is RECONCILED_ACCEPTED with negativeDeliveryEvidence=true, preserving proof that submission occurred without pretending delivery succeeded.
NOT_FOUND classification removed from Postal reconciliation so webhook absence cannot release a resend.
